{
  "name": "Pipeline Dependencies Explained",
  "overview": "Pipeline dependencies in this repo are implemented at two levels: **within-DAG** task ordering driven by JSON config, and **cross-DAG** chaining via Airflow sensors and triggers with same-day execution-date resolution.",
  "plan": "# How Pipeline Dependencies Are Implemented\n\nThis repo uses **Apache Airflow DAGs** (not CI/CD pipelines). Dependencies are split into **intra-DAG** (tasks inside one DAG) and **inter-DAG** (ordering across separate DAGs).\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TB\n  subgraph entry [Manual entry point]\n    leave[leave_data DAG]\n  end\n\n  subgraph parallel [Can run in parallel]\n    leave\n    onsite[onsite_employee DAG]\n  end\n\n  leave --\u003e|ExternalTaskSensor wait_leave_data| emp[employee_data DAG]\n  onsite --\u003e|ExternalTaskSensor wait_onsite_employee| emp\n  onsite --\u003e|after end: wait_leave then trigger| emp\n\n  emp --\u003e|TriggerDagRunOperator| saal[saal_model DAG]\n\n  hr[employee_hr_data DAG]\n  hr -.-\u003e|no cross-DAG link today| saal\n```\n\n---\n\n## 1. Within-DAG dependencies (config-driven)\n\nEach pipeline reads a JSON config from S3 (e.g. [`employee_data/config/employee_data.json`](employee_data/config/employee_data.json)) that includes `airflow-task-dependencies-details`.\n\n### Config format (used today)\n\nEvery current config uses the **linear chain** form:\n\n```json\n\"airflow-task-dependencies-details\": {\n  \"employee-data\": [\"start\", \"end\"]\n}\n```\n\nMeaning: `start` → `employee-data` (TaskGroup) → `end`.\n\nThe same pattern exists in [`leave_data.json`](employee_data/config/leave_data.json), [`onsite_employee.json`](employee_data/config/onsite_employee.json), and [`employee_hr_data.json`](employee_data/config/employee_hr_data.json).\n\n### How the DAG builder wires it\n\nShared logic lives in `DagCommons._build_parent_child_dependencies()` — duplicated identically in each flow module ([`employee_data.py`](employee_data/flows/employee_data.py), [`leave_data_flow.py`](employee_data/flows/leave_data_flow.py), etc.).\n\n**Step A — Build task groups from config**\n\n`build_task_group()` iterates `airflow-task-details` and creates one `TaskGroup` per top-level key (e.g. `employee-data`). Inside each group:\n\n- Spark jobs become a **linear sub-chain**: `spark-submit` → `spark-monitor` (see [`build_spark_details`](employee_data/flows/employee_data.py) around lines 566–568 and 485–486).\n- Trino steps (if any) are appended similarly.\n\n**Step B — Ensure boundary dummy tasks**\n\nIf not already present, the builder injects:\n\n- `start` — `DummyOperator` at the front\n- `end` — `DummyOperator` at the back\n\n**Step C — Apply config dependencies**\n\nTwo supported config shapes:\n\n| Format | Example | Behavior |\n|--------|---------|----------|\n| **Linear chain** (current) | `\"task-a\": [\"start\", \"end\"]` | `task-a.set_upstream(start)` and `task-a.set_downstream(end)` |\n| **Parent-child map** (supported, unused) | `\"parent-child-relation\": { \"child\": [\"parent1\", \"parent2\"] }` | Multiple parents → one child via `\u003e\u003e` edges |\n\nFor the linear form, missing node names (`start`, `end`) are auto-created as dummy operators.\n\n**Resulting within-DAG graph (typical single Spark group)**\n\n```\nstart → employee-data.spark-submit → employee-data.spark-monitor → end\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Cross-DAG dependencies (hard-coded in flow modules)\n\nCross-DAG ordering is **not** in JSON config. It is declared explicitly at the bottom of each DAG file using Airflow operators.\n\n### Shared helper: [`pipeline_chain.py`](employee_data/flows/pipeline_chain.py)\n\nManual triggers often use different `logical_date` values even on the same calendar day. Default Airflow `ExternalTaskSensor` matching would fail.\n\n`upstream_sensor_kwargs()` centralizes sensor settings:\n\n- `mode=\"poke\"`, 60s interval, 2h timeout\n- Custom `execution_date_fn` from `same_day_latest_success_execution_date_fn()`\n\nThat function:\n\n1. Converts the current run’s `logical_date` to **Asia/Dubai** day boundaries\n2. Queries `DagRun` + `TaskInstance` for the latest **SUCCESS** upstream run on that calendar day\n3. Returns that run’s `execution_date`, or falls back to the current `logical_date` if none found\n\nThis lets downstream DAGs wait for upstream success **by day**, not by exact timestamp.\n\n### [`leave_data`](employee_data/flows/leave_data_flow.py)\n\n- **No cross-DAG dependencies** — entry point when the chain is started manually\n- Only the config-driven `start → leave-data → end` graph\n\n### [`onsite_employee`](employee_data/flows/onsite_employee_flow.py)\n\nAfter the DAG’s own work finishes:\n\n```python\nend \u003e\u003e wait_leave \u003e\u003e trigger_employee_data\n```\n\n- `wait_leave_data` — `ExternalTaskSensor` on `leave_data.end`\n- `trigger_employee_data` — `TriggerDagRunOperator` fires `employee_data` with the same `logical_date` (`wait_for_completion=False`)\n\nSo `onsite_employee` can run in parallel with `leave_data`, but only triggers `employee_data` after `leave_data` has succeeded.\n\n### [`employee_data`](employee_data/flows/employee_data.py)\n\nBefore work starts, it waits for both upstream ingest DAGs:\n\n```python\n[wait_leave, wait_onsite] \u003e\u003e start\n```\n\nAfter work completes, it kicks off dbt:\n\n```python\nend \u003e\u003e trigger_saal_model\n```\n\n- Sensors wait on `leave_data.end` and `onsite_employee.end`\n- `trigger_saal_model` — `TriggerDagRunOperator` for `saal_model` (`reset_dag_run=True`)\n\n### [`employee_hr_data`](employee_data/flows/employee_hr_data_flow.py)\n\n- **Standalone** — config-only `start → employee-hr-data → end`\n- No `ExternalTaskSensor` or `TriggerDagRunOperator` today\n\n### [`saal_model`](employee_data/flows/...)\n\n- Triggered by `employee_data`; not defined with upstream sensors in this repo’s employee ingest flows\n\n---\n\n## 3. End-to-end execution order\n\nWhen the chain is started from `onsite_employee` (or manually in the right order):\n\n1. **`leave_data`** and **`onsite_employee`** can run concurrently (if both are triggered)\n2. **`onsite_employee.end`** → waits for **`leave_data.end`** → triggers **`employee_data`**\n3. **`employee_data`** waits for both **`leave_data`** and **`onsite_employee`** before `start`, then runs Spark ingest\n4. **`employee_data.end`** → triggers **`saal_model`**\n5. **`employee_hr_data`** is independent unless manually coordinated\n\n---\n\n## 4. Design split (important)\n\n| Concern | Where it lives | How to change |\n|---------|----------------|---------------|\n| Task order inside a DAG | S3 JSON `airflow-task-dependencies-details` | Edit config; redeploy config to S3 |\n| Spark step order inside a group | Python `build_task_group()` loop | Code change in flow module |\n| Cross-DAG wait/trigger | Bottom of flow `.py` files | Code change + DAG sync to Airflow |\n| Same-day sensor matching | [`pipeline_chain.py`](employee_data/flows/pipeline_chain.py) | Shared helper used by sensors |\n\nThere is **no single orchestrator DAG**. Chaining is **distributed**: each downstream DAG declares what it waits for, and some upstream DAGs proactively trigger the next step.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Related folder name: `dependencies/`\n\nThe [`employee_data/dependencies/scripts/`](employee_data/dependencies/scripts/) folder holds **PySpark job scripts** uploaded to MinIO — not Airflow dependency definitions. The word “dependencies” here means runtime job artifacts (JAR classpath, PySpark mains), separate from DAG task ordering.\n"
}
